ThingDef.label: ullavess
ThingDef.description: A group of tall tapering vessels standing mouth-up, each half-full of clear fluid you can see into. The outer wall is veined maroon over yellow-green; the rim is a hard iridescent lip and the inside wall is glassy and visibly slick. Spent vessels below are brown and collapsed. Ullavess is the clade's anchor — the plant a player recognises as a predator on sight — and a cloudy vessel means it has fed recently.

ThingDef.label: nemreth
ThingDef.description: A low mat of hair-fine red stalks, each ending in a clear glistening bead that holds the light like dew and never dries. From a distance the whole mat glitters; close up, the beads are thick and drawn into threads, and older stalks are curled inward around what they caught. The most beautiful thing in the biome that is also a killer, and it never pretended otherwise — its adhesive is the luxury attar's binder.

ThingDef.label: velluric
ThingDef.description: Above the channel, one small pale flower on a thin stalk, unremarkable. Everything else is submerged: a drifting mass of fine bladders, each with an inward trapdoor, invisible from the bank. The water above a velluric bed is very slightly clearer than the water beside it — the tell, and the only warning a small thing crossing it ever gets. ⚠️ Ships here as a shore/shallow plant, the same as any other wild plant; a true underwater growth habit is UNMEASURABLE without a Desktop pass against the RM_DiveEligible terrain work (mandrake.rm.divinginteraction) and is owed as a follow-on, not this pass.

ThingDef.label: braskeen
ThingDef.description: A flat whorl lying on the surface, each arm ending in a pair of hinged blades held slightly open, fringed with stiff interlocking teeth. The blades close when something touches them and stay shut for a day with the catch showing between the teeth. Blade interiors are a raw wet pink. The only plant on the page with real motion — a channel of these snapping shut one after another as scuttlers cross is the biome's best ambient moment.

ThingDef.label: ommolyn
ThingDef.description: Above the mud, a single modest cream flower on a short stalk and a few limp surface leaves. Below, a buried maze of forked hollow tubes lined with inward-pointing hairs that admit and never release. Nothing on the surface suggests it — but the mud within a tile or two is conspicuously free of scuttlers, and that absence is the tell. Its tube-fibre is the only cordage that survives the brine.
